transcript:
Header:
2026-06-07 09:21 UTC | Duration: 42m | Recording ID: FLY-20260607-QL-0921
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Daniel (CTO QuarryLane), Renee (Head of Security), Omar (Cloud Arch), Elisa (Legal)

Summary:
Quick intake to understand QuarryLane's security gating for any hosted inference provider. Main asks: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO via Okta SAML, fine-grained RBAC, audit logs and retention policy (7 years regulatory question), and options for encryption/KMS including customer-managed keys and HSM. Discussion of tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and Private (VPC/on-prem).

---
00:00 Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood, i'll kick it, quick intros.
00:08 Daniel: hey, daniel here, CTO, keeping it short we evaluate infra and security, excited to understand hosting options.
00:13 Renee: renee, head of security, mainly here for compliance and data residency questions.
00:18 Omar: omar, cloud architect, i'll look at networking and key mgmt.
00:22 Priya: priya, solutions eng, i'll take notes on integration paths.
00:27 Liam: liam on se side, happy to go deep on KMS and perf.

00:40 Maya: cool quick framing, we support three deployment modes - hosted api, dedicated reserved capacity, private (vpc or on prem) — each has different controls. which of these are you leaning toward?
00:55 Daniel: our initial p.o.c. we'd like hosted to move fast but security is first. if hosted can't meet controls we need dedicated or private.
01:05 Renee: SOC2 is table stakes, do you have an up to date report? also iso27001 would be great.
01:12 Maya: yes we are SOC2 Type II, last attestation was 2025 Q4, we also maintain ISO 27001 cert, we can share evidence pack — I'll send the report.
01:20 Elisa: legal will want to see the scoping / subservice org chart, is that included?
01:26 Maya: yep we include scoping and control mappings in the pack.

02:05 Omar: on SSO, we run Okta and we prefer IdP-initiated SAML, can Redwood support SAML metadata exchange and Just-In-Time provisioning?
02:15 Liam: yes, SAML SSO supported for both hosted and dedicated; we support SP-initiated and IdP-initiated, JIT provisioning for users is supported today, we also have SAML assertions mapping to roles for RBAC.
02:26 Renee: about RBAC, we need fine grained controls - separation between developers, analysts, and ops, plus audit trail for role changes. is that possible with hosted?
02:36 Priya: hosted offers RBAC integrated with SSO and team/org constructs. for enterprise customers we expose SCIM for provisioning and audit logs with token-level attribution.
02:48 Omar: SCIM + SAML mapping is good. question: can we restrict certain models or routes to specific teams, e.g. PII-sensitive routes only on dedicated instances?
03:02 Liam: yes, route-level policies exist. you can pin models to dedicated pools and set fallback policies. we also support per-route enforcement so you can restrict model families or exposures.

04:10 Daniel: encryption at rest, we want customer-managed keys. do you support KMS integration with our cloud KMS, and HSM-backed keys for higher assurance?
04:22 Maya: hosted supports customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and GCP KMS — you can rotate keys and we support envelope encryption. for HSM-backed keys (BYOK with external HSM) that's available as part of Private deployments or enterprise Dedicated with an add-on.
04:40 Renee: do audit logs include key use events? we need key usage logs for forensics.
04:46 Liam: yes audit logs capture key operations that are proxied through the service. note: for hosted with CMK, final decrypt still happens in our runtime but with envelope keys; for Private installation with BYOK the customer controls the key lifecycle and logs remain in your environment.

06:00 Elisa: data retention - we have compliance to keep transactional logs for 7 years and must be able to apply legal holds. how does Redwood handle retention and deletions?
06:10 Priya: we expose retention policies per-tenant. default retention for logs is 90 days for hosted, but enterprise packages allow longer retention. for customer data used in inference you can request longer legal retention or export; private deployments let you keep everything on-prem.
06:25 Renee: 90 days isn't going to cut it for our audit requirements. can dedicated be configured to retain audit logs longer, and can logs be forwarded to our SIEM?
06:33 Liam: dedicated supports configurable retention and we offer log-forwarding to S3/Cloud Storage or syslog->SIEM. we'll share the ingestion spec.

08:00 Daniel: network isolation — can hosted traffic be egress-restricted so that keys and PII don't leave region? and what about VPC peering for Dedicated?
08:14 Omar: we want control over egress routes, and need a private link option.
08:18 Maya: hosted supports region pinning and private networking via managed private endpoints. Dedicated comes with VPC peering or private link options, Private obviously sits in your VPC or on-prem. we'll send VPC architecture diagrams.

10:05 Renee: incident response and breach notification SLA? we need notify windows and forensics support.
10:12 Maya: standard is 72-hour notification; enterprise SLA shortens that and includes a dedicated incident contact, forensic logs, and a post-incident report. we can include those terms in the contract.

12:30 Omar: curious about multi-tenancy isolation in Hosted — cognitive leak risk between tenants?
12:37 Liam: runtime has strong tenant isolation via container and model instance separation, plus KV cache partitioning. that said, for highest assurance dedicated or private is recommended. we've done workload isolation tests — we can share the whitepaper and the test results.
12:52 Daniel: would like that whitepaper.

14:00 Renee: encryption in transit — mutual TLS?
14:06 Priya: mTLS supported for private/dedicated; hosted uses TLS1.3 with per-connection certs and supports client certs for private endpoints.

16:00 Elisa: contractually we need subcontractor lists and data flow diagrams.
16:06 Maya: included in the security pack, plus SOC2 scoping lists.

18:30 Omar: for a POC we want to run a 2-week dedicated pilot with our sample workload and measure p95 latency under 128 token bursts and also verify SAML provisioning and log forwarding. what's typical onboarding time?
18:45 Liam: for dedicated pilot it's usually 5-7 days to stand up a reserved pool if capacity available; can be faster with our standard configs. for hosted POC it's immediate.
19:00 Daniel: cost perspective — dedicated commit vs hosted per-token?
19:07 Maya: we'll share a cost comparison sheet; quick note, dedicated reduces per-token unit costs and gives consistent latency while hosted is easier to start.

21:00 Renee: can you guarantee data residency for EU data?
21:06 Maya: yes, we have region pinning and EU region hosting; for regulatory requirements we recommend Dedicated or Private to avoid cross-region failover if that's not allowed.

23:20 Omar: any SOC2/ISO exceptions or open findings currently?
23:25 Maya: nothing material open; we'll include the AICPA bridge letter and our remediation timeline in the pack.

25:30 Priya: quick demo option — we can show SAML talk through and RBAC mapping next week in a 60-min tech deep dive.
25:38 Daniel: that would be useful, please include our Okta admin in invites.

27:10 Elisa: what about data deletion guarantees - can you scrub prompt/response logs on demand?
27:17 Liam: yes for enterprise accounts we support on-demand deletes and can provide deletion receipts; for hosted free-tier there may be delays.

29:00 Renee: audit log fidelity - do logs include token-level attribution and model version?
29:06 Priya: yes logs include request id, user identity, model version, route, and timestamps. we also include p99 latencies and error traces when enabled.

31:40 Omar: one more on KMS - we have a hybrid architecture, keys in our AWS KMS but would like HSM backed keys for certain datasets. path forward?
31:52 Liam: we recommend Private deployment for full HSM control; otherwise dedicated with a secure tunnel to your HSM can be arranged as an enterprise integration. we'll map out the integration patterns.

34:00 Maya: quick recap: we'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts, network diagrams, whitepaper on tenant isolation, dedicated pilot plan + perf test, and the cost comparison.
34:12 Daniel: good. timeline — we'd like to decide on a vendor by end of Q3, pilot in July.
34:20 Maya: sounds good, we'll prioritize the pack and get the technical deep dive scheduled.

36:30 Renee: legal question — do you accept data processing addendums with our specific clauses on data residency and subprocessors?
36:40 Maya: yes we have a standard DPA and are open to mutual negotiation for enterprise customers. we'll flag legal for redwood.

39:00 Elisa: i'll need the DPA and subcontractor list.
39:06 Maya: will send.

41:00 Maya: alright thanks everyone we'll follow up with materials and set up the deep dive, thanks.

---
